newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli warplanes rocket Hizbollah targets.
newsitem.headline: Israeli warplanes rocket Hizbollah targets.

text.p: Israeli warplanes rocketed suspected Islamic guerrilla targets in south Lebanon highlands on Friday, security sources said.

They said the planes fired at least eight rockets in two bombing runs into Iqlim al-Toufah mountain ridge controlled by pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas just north of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
There was no immediate word on casualties in the air attack, the first Israeli raid into Lebanon in 1997.

Shortly afterwards, Hizbollah said in a statement that a group of its fighters attacked an Israeli position at Beir Kallab on the edge of the zone in the early morning, causing a number of casualties.
A second group of guerrillas firing machineguns and anti-tank rockets attacked two other Israeli outposts at Sojoud and Kassaret al-Ouroush, the militant group added.
On Thursday, guerrillas set off a roadside bomb near a patrol of the Israeli-allied South Lebanon Army (SLA) in the zone, wounding three militiamen.
Hizbollah is fighting to oust some 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 SLA militia from the border occupation zone set up in south Lebanon in 1985 to ward off guerrilla raids on northern Israel.
